subject: Private & Dedicated: isolation overview and control legend for SOC 2/SIG review
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridian.com>

Cc: Auditus SOC-ops <soc2@auditus.co>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: annotated isolation legend + mapping for SOC 2/SIG

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the quick discussion last week. As part of Veridian's SOC 2 scoping we're asking vendors for a focused pack covering network isolation and tenant separation for both your Hosted/Dedicated and Private deployment options.

Two asks to start our SIG/CIF review:
- An "isolation legend" that annotates which lanes/boxes on your topology maps correspond to controls (e.g., control-plane separation, customer VPC boundary, egress proxies, KMS enclaves).
- A simple control-to-artifact mapping (which diagram + log or evidence artifact demonstrates each control).

Can you share a draft PDF and a CSV mapping we can ingest into our review tracker? We're aiming to complete first-pass review by Aug 6. Auditus is copied on this thread; they will ingest any artifacts into the SIG questionnaire.

If anything needs clarification, Kim from your security team can loop in infra.

Best,
Ellen

--
Ellen Park
Director, Infrastructure Security

Thanks Michael — I've uploaded a first-pass control mapping and a representative network snapshot to the Drive folder. Attaching the two files here for your convenience (control_mapping_table.csv, network_snapshot.png).

Notes and deviations to call out for the SIG reviewers:
- The legend enumerates three isolation tiers across Dedicated/Private:
  * Tier A: Customer-dedicated GPU pools + customer VPC peering (strong tenant fencing, KMS per-tenant policy).
  * Tier B: Shared-hosted control plane but isolated KV/cache prefixes + request-level encryption.
  * Tier C: Edge transit proxies that terminate TLS and perform per-tenant routing.

- Evidence mapping: we've referenced Docs and log artifacts by artifact id in the CSV; for most items a redacted sample (log slice, audit entry) is sufficient.

Question for Veridian/Auditus: control SIG-3 (airgap/airlock evidence) — do you need a fully air-gapped build record for Private deployments or will network ACLs + documented operational process suffice for now? If you need the stricter artefact we can schedule an internal capture window but that will shift the deliverable by ~5 business days.

Ellen / Auditus —

Deliverables attached: isolation_legend_v2.pdf (annotated legend + two-page narrative) and the control mapping CSV and snapshot (previously uploaded). Summary below:

Summary highlights:
- The attached legend annotates the diagram elements we typically show in our private deployment topology: control-plane cluster (customer-managed control plane endpoints), dedicated GPU tenant ring, KMS boundary, egress proxy clusters, and optional airlock zones.
- Mapping table includes artifact ids (LOG-xxxx for audit logs, DOC-xxxx for runbooks, DS-xxxx for signed DocuSign artifacts).
- For initial SIG intake we recommend a representative US Private snapshot. If you require region-specific artifacts (EU), tell us and we'll produce the equivalent set.

On the airgap question (SIG-3): per Auditus guidance last cycle, a documented operational process + network ACL snapshots and a redacted build attest are acceptable for scope; if Veridian needs a fully isolated offline build demonstration we will schedule the capture and update artifacts (est +5 business days).

Next steps / asks:
- Ellen: confirm whether US-only snapshot is sufficient or if you need EU artifacts.
- Auditus: please confirm receipt and whether the CSV format works for ingestion.

Thanks,
Michael

Attachments: isolation_legend_v2.pdf
